markers.title: The page opens with its exceptions, not its total
markers.decision: The sub-line reads 14 products, 2 safety data sheets expiring within 30 days, 1 missing. A register is only interesting where it is wrong, so the two numbers that need work are stated before anything is clicked.
markers.rejected: A compliance percentage. It is one number that hides which product is the problem and reads as a score to be defended.
markers.pattern: Design system: page head with a factual sub-line (p-page-head)

markers.title: Filters that state the number they will filter to
markers.decision: Each chip carries its own count, so the exceptions are visible before the filter is used and the manager can see there is nothing to do without doing anything. The counts are tinted with the same warning and danger tokens the badges use further down the table.
markers.rejected: A plain filter dropdown. It hides the counts behind an interaction and gives the page nothing to say at rest.
markers.pattern: Slite, knowledge management with filter chips — https://mobbin.com/screens/784fd37d-3429-4f47-b58c-0b6fc0ffed07

markers.title: The audit is a fact on the page, with what it covered
markers.decision: Last audit 2 Sep by Priya M., 14 of 14 products sighted. Naming the person and the coverage turns an audit from a status into something a reader can check, and it makes a partial audit visible rather than rounding it up to done.
markers.rejected: A green Compliant badge. It says less and it cannot be wrong in a useful way.
markers.pattern: Design system: meta line aligned to the filter row (p-meta)

markers.title: The protective equipment is in the row, not in the document
markers.decision: Gloves, goggles and apron appear as labelled chips on every row. It is the one fact somebody needs before they touch the product, and putting it in the table means it is answered without opening anything.
markers.rejected: A hazard pictogram alone. It is the regulated symbol and it does not tell a new starter what to put on.

markers.title: An expiry says what to do about it
markers.finding: Team members said they had never been told the threshold for reporting, so each person sets their own.
markers.decision: The research kept finding people left to interpret something nobody had explained to them. So the expiring row does not stop at a date and a colour. It says 16 days, then ask the supplier for the new sheet. The status and the next action sit in the same cell.
markers.rejected: The expiry date on its own. It is accurate, it is the compliance fact, and it leaves the manager to work out whose job it is.
markers.pattern: Airtable, status pill with a date beneath — https://mobbin.com/screens/7d6333cb-c4c4-4ce0-a1e0-9d130d16eb02

markers.title: Spill steps are a column, because a spill is not a reading task
markers.decision: Every product carries a direct link to its three spill steps. The steps are written in the panel in plain words, and the second one names the spill kit by its marker number on the emergency information plan, so the two modules point at the same physical object.
markers.rejected: Burying the procedure inside the safety data sheet. It is where the law puts it and it is fifteen pages from the part somebody needs.
markers.pattern: Navattic, table row opening a detail panel — https://mobbin.com/screens/a99e7d4b-d709-4f0c-94b8-8ff2eb174f65

markers.title: A missing sheet says how it got that way
markers.decision: The missing row reads Added 28 Aug without a sheet. Naming the moment the gap was created points at the process that allowed it, which is the fix, rather than at the person holding the register today.
markers.rejected: A red Non-compliant badge. It grades the restaurant and says nothing about how to stop it happening again.
markers.pattern: Design system: danger badge with a supporting line (p-badge p-badge-danger)
